facts.text: Jackpot was founded after Idaho outlawed casino gaming in 1954, when Cactus Pete and Don French moved slot machines across the state line.
The town’s name came from a compromise between two club owners, settling on 'Jackpot' in 1959 after earlier names like Horse Shu.
Jackpot sits just under 5,200 feet above sea level, nestled near Salmon Falls Creek and north of Middle Stack Mountain in the Granite Range.
A public library in Jackpot serves as a branch of the Elko-Lander-Eureka County Library System, offering community resources.
In 2003, a CSI episode was set in Jackpot, though filming took place in Fawnskin, California, highlighting the town’s quirky appeal.
The original casino clubs, Cactus Pete's and Horseshu, later merged into Ameristar Casinos, forming the backbone of Jackpot’s economy.
